items.title: Three Conditions That Make These Causes Actually Grow, and What Each Ripening Mark Is Good For

items.zh: 又此諸因略由三緣而得增長，能感圓滿增上廣大異熟令起。何等三緣？一、心清淨，二、加行清淨，三、田清淨。
items.en: These causes, in brief, grow through three further conditions, able to bring about a ripening that is complete, ever-increasing, and vast: first, purity of mind; second, purity of practice; third, purity of the field.

items.zh: 若於無上正等菩提清淨意樂，用彼善根決定迴向猛利意樂，純厚廣大淨信修行，見同法者深生歡喜，日夜剎那於多隨法隨尋、隨伺，名心清淨。即於其中長時數習無間所作、常委所作，他於此善若未受行，讚美令受；若已受行，讚美令喜。即於如是所有善根，安處建立，名加行清淨。當知略說能正發起如是加行，及正安住此加行果，名田清淨。云何異熟果？
謂諸菩薩壽量具足故，能於長時修習善品，依自他利積集增長無量善根，是名菩薩壽量具足果。若諸菩薩形色具足故，大眾愛樂；眾愛樂故，咸共歸仰。如是形色可愛樂故，一切大眾咸歸仰故，凡所發言無不聽用，是名菩薩形色具足果。
items.en: Because of complete longevity, a bodhisattva is able to cultivate wholesome practices over a long span of time, accumulating boundless wholesome roots for the benefit of self and others alike — this is the fruit of complete longevity … because of fine appearance, the multitude delights in and takes refuge in such a bodhisattva; and because of this, whatever they say is universally heeded — this is the fruit of fine appearance.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩族姓具足故，大眾尊敬供養稱讚；眾所尊敬供養稱讚故，於彼彼事勸諸眾生精勤修學，無不敬用速疾修行，無違無犯；是名菩薩族姓具足果。若諸菩薩自在具足故，能以布施攝諸眾生，速令成熟，是名菩薩自在具足果。若諸菩薩信言具足故，能以愛語、利行、同事攝諸眾生，速令成熟，是名菩薩信言具足果。若諸菩薩大勢具足故，於諸眾生種種事業皆能營助，施布恩德；由此恩德感眾生心，彼知恩故，咸來歸仰；所出言教，速疾隨轉恭敬信用；是名菩薩大勢具足果。若諸菩薩人性具足故，成就男根，堪為一切勝功德器；能於一切所作事業，思擇一切所知境界，都無所畏無礙而行。一切有情於一切時皆來臻赴同共集會，屏處、露處言論同止，受用飲食皆無嫌礙。是名菩薩人性具足果。若諸菩薩大力具足故，於能引攝善法加行，及能饒益有情加行，皆無厭倦，勇猛精進、堅固精進，速證通慧，是名菩薩大力具足果。若諸菩薩成就如是八種異熟，具八種果，能善饒益一切有情，隨順生起一切佛法。菩薩安住異熟果中，於諸有情種種眾多利益事業，自有力能；及善安處所化有情，彼於自事隨順而作；如是乃名隨其所欲所作成辦。

items.title: Section: Power Without Skill Fails, Skill Without Power Fails — And Why a Bodhisattva's Wandering Is Never Wasted

items.zh: 若諸菩薩自有力能，不善安處所化有情，彼於自事不隨順作；如是於他所作利益不名熾盛、不名隨順。由是因緣，不名能作他利益事。若諸菩薩自無力能，而善安處所化有情，彼於自事隨順而作；如是於他所作利益不名熾盛、不名隨順。由是因緣，不名能作他利益事。是故菩薩要具二事，方於有情所作利益名為熾盛、名為隨順。
items.en: If a bodhisattva has the capacity but is not skilled at properly settling those to be guided, so that they do not follow through with what benefits them, then the benefit rendered to others cannot be called flourishing or genuinely realised … if a bodhisattva is skilled at properly settling those to be guided but lacks the capacity … this too cannot be called genuinely benefiting others … for this reason, a bodhisattva must possess both together before benefiting beings can be called flourishing and genuinely realised.

items.zh: 由是因緣，乃名能作他利益事。如是菩薩住異熟果，自能成熟一切佛法，亦能令他於三乘道隨其所應速得成熟；又能令自速證無上正等菩提，亦能令他已成熟者速得解脫。
由諸菩薩安住八種異熟果中，能使有情利益安樂，是故一切有情所處空無義利無始生死，菩薩處之，能令不空，有大義利。
items.en: Because bodhisattvas, abiding in these eight ripened fruits, are able to bring beings benefit and happiness — where ordinary beings' beginningless wandering through birth and death is empty, devoid of genuine meaning — a bodhisattva's own presence within that very cycle is never empty, but carries great and genuine meaning.

blocks.text: How these qualities grow, and what each makes possible. A passage (0485a05) is untranslated.
"Purity of mind; purity of practice; purity of the field." Master Cháng Bǎi: the field is the recipient; mind and practice are oneself.
"Because of complete longevity, a bodhisattva is able to cultivate wholesome practices over a long span." "Because of fine appearance, the multitude delights" to come near.

Through **noble birth**, people revere one and readily follow one's encouragement to practise. Through **authority**, one can gather beings by generosity. Through **credibility**, one gathers them by kind words, beneficial action, and shared purpose. Through **influence**, one helps beings in their affairs, and grateful, they listen. Through **manhood** (in the treatise's own terms), one can go anywhere, meet anyone, without hindrance. Through **strength**, one never tires of effort for good and for beings, and swiftly attains higher knowledge.
"If a bodhisattva has capacity but is not skilled at settling those to be guided, the benefit cannot be called genuine"; and skill without capacity also fails. Both are needed.
"Where ordinary beings' beginningless wandering is empty, devoid of meaning, a bodhisattva's presence within that very cycle is never empty." Venerable Miào Jìng comments.

quiz.q: The causes grow through three conditions; first, "purity of mind." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
quiz.why: "First, purity of mind; second, purity of practice; third, purity of the field." Venerable Miào Jìng: what is purity of mind? Having pure faith.

quiz.q: The third, "purity of the field" — what does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: mind and practice both pure, practice accomplished — naturally a field of merit worthy of offerings
quiz.why: "Third, purity of the field." Master Cháng Bǎi: third, purity of the field — mind and practice both pure, practice accomplished, one is naturally beings' field of merit, worthy of their offerings.

quiz.q: "Having capacity but not skilled at settling those to be guided." What is the lack, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: unable to guide beings with the four means of gathering
quiz.why: "If a bodhisattva has the capacity but is not skilled at properly settling those to be guided, so that they do not follow through with what benefits them." Venerable Miào Jìng: it means being unable to guide beings with the four means of gathering.

quiz.q: "Ordinary beings' beginningless wandering is empty, devoid of meaning." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: beings in the world achieve nothing at all
quiz.why: "Where ordinary beings' beginningless wandering through birth and death is empty, devoid of genuine meaning — a bodhisattva's own presence within that very cycle is never empty." Venerable Miào Jìng: beings in the world are "empty, without benefit" — no achievement at all.
